record.original_question: For each thickness t, what is the maximum possible chromatic number of a graph of thickness t?

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 What is the maximum chromatic number among all graphs of thickness t?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The thickness of a graph $G$, denoted $\theta(G)$, is the minimum number of planar subgraphs into which the edge set of $G$ can be partitioned. The chromatic number $\chi(G)$ is the minimum number of colors needed to properly color the vertices of $G$ so that adjacent vertices receive different colors.

For each positive integer $t$, define
$$f(t) = \sup\{\chi(G) : G \text{ is a finite simple graph with } \theta(G) \le t\}.$$

Determine $f(t)$ for every $t \ge 1$. In particular, find the exact value (or improve the known bounds) of the maximum chromatic number attainable by a graph of thickness $t$. (Known elementary bounds give $f(t) \le 6t$ via degeneracy, and one has $f(1)=4$ by the Four Color Theorem; for $t=2$ it is known that $9 \le f(2) \le 12$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is open even for thickness 2 (the Earth–Moon problem posed by Ringel in 1959), where the chromatic number is known to lie between 9 and 12, with Gethner conjecturing 11. For larger thickness $t$, only the general degeneracy upper bound $6t$ and various lower bounds are known; the exact value of $f(t)$ remains unknown.

status_evidence.title: Earth–Moon problem - HandWiki
status_evidence.snippet: The Earth–Moon problem is an unsolved problem on graph coloring... It is known that the answer is at least 9 and at most 12.
status_evidence.claim: The thickness-2 case (Earth–Moon problem) remains unsolved with bounds 9 ≤ χ ≤ 12.

status_evidence.title: Thickness (graph theory) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Largest chromatic number of any thickness-2 graph remains an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The maximum chromatic number among thickness-2 graphs is unresolved.
